ai.mechanism: Evidence shows only that contract 0xd3ec0e34aa628c66083759fe35e45ccf73a76d28 on Base had its entire USDC balance (share 1.0) moved out in a single transaction. The packet contains no call trace, caller privilege data, role or initialisation events, oracle inputs or protocol identification, so no exploit mechanism can be named.
ai.lossBearer: Unidentified: whoever holds claim on the USDC in 0xd3ec0e34aa628c66083759fe35e45ccf73a76d28. No protocol, depositor set or integrator is shown in the evidence.
ai.narrative: A contract on Base was emptied of its full USDC balance, 789,437.589056 USDC (~$789,438), in one transaction. That is the whole of the evidence. There is nothing here that distinguishes an exploit from a treasury sweep, a bridge settlement or a planned migration: no caller, no permission check, no owner change, no protocol name, and no list of integrators or depositors who would carry the loss. The note attached to the packet says as much. Without a named mechanism and a named loss bearer, there is no supportable loss path to trade against, so this is flagged unknown and vetoed pending more data.
